**How to use this module:** Each activity takes approximately 10–25 minutes, with longer optional extensions. Choose an activity that fits your current work; you do not need to complete them in order. Keep your outputs in a notebook or project folder so your decisions remain traceable.

## A seven-session writing experiment {#writing-habits}

**Connected guide:** [Developing a Writing Habit](writing-habits.qmd)

**Task:** Choose a low-pressure writing unit (for example 10 minutes). Before each session, record your purpose; after, record what you produced and the next action. At the end, assess which cues and conditions worked.

**Suggested record:** Session date | Purpose | Time or output | What helped | Next action.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Compare note-taking approaches {#note-taking}

**Connected guide:** [Purposeful Note Taking](note-taking.qmd)

**Task:** Read a short environmental article twice. On the first pass, use Cornell-style notes; on the second, annotate claims and limitations. Compare what each approach helped you notice.

**Suggested record:** Source | Reading purpose | Factual notes | Questions | Interpretation.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Reverse-outline a draft {#outlining}

**Connected guide:** [Outlining and Reverse Outlining](outlining.qmd)

**Task:** Select 5–8 consecutive paragraphs from your own draft or an openly available article. Write a one-line job description for each. Mark repetition or gaps and propose a better order.

**Suggested record:** Paragraph | Main job | Evidence used | Move / revise / keep.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Audit five citations {#reference-managers}

**Connected guide:** [Reference Managers](reference-managers.qmd)

**Task:** Import five sources into a reference manager. Verify each record against the source itself, group the items in a collection, and create a bibliography. Check the exported citations.

**Suggested record:** Source identifier | Metadata verified? | Collection / tags | Correction made.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Run three documented search iterations {#literature-search}

**Connected guide:** [Reproducible Literature Searching](literature-search.qmd)

**Task:** State a focused question. Run three searches, changing just one element per iteration; log exact queries, platform, date, filters, and screening decisions.

**Suggested record:** Date | Database | Exact query | Filters | Results | Change and reason.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Move from a matrix to a paragraph {#literature-synthesis}

**Connected guide:** [Synthesizing Literature](literature-synthesis.qmd)

**Task:** Read three sources addressing one shared question. Compare evidence and methods, identify a pattern and a limitation, then write one synthesis paragraph with citations.

**Suggested record:** Source | Context | Method | Finding | Limitation | Connection.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Translate for two audiences {#science-communication}

**Connected guide:** [Communicating with Non-Expert Audiences](science-communication.qmd)

**Task:** Take one clearly supported scientific claim and rewrite it for a community meeting and for an interdisciplinary research team. Compare choices about vocabulary, emphasis, uncertainty, and format.

**Suggested record:** Audience | Goal | Key message | Terms to explain | Evidence / uncertainty.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Feedback to revision plan {#peer-review}

**Connected guide:** [Peer Review and Revision](peer-review.qmd)

**Task:** Use a short draft. Ask a peer for one reader takeaway, two substantive comments, and one unanswered question. Convert feedback into prioritized revision actions.

**Suggested record:** Feedback | Location | Priority | Planned action | Reason.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Trace a claim and audit tool use {#research-ethics}

**Connected guide:** [Ethical Research, Writing, and AI Use](research-ethics.qmd)

**Task:** Select one paragraph and one image from a draft. Verify provenance, permissions, citation, and accuracy. Record any assisted tools and whether the material could be shared safely.

**Suggested record:** Item | Source / permission | Verification | Risk | Action.

**Reflect:** What did this activity make visible that you might otherwise have missed? What would you change in your next attempt?

---

## Practice reflection

After any activity, record three things: what you tried, what you noticed, and what you will do next. The goal is a usable process, not a perfect worksheet.
